definition: A neural network that uses learned filters sliding over its input, especially effective for images and other grid data.
details: Convolutions share weights across spatial locations and build hierarchical features, from edges in early layers to whole objects in later ones. LeNet demonstrated the approach on handwritten digits, and deeper CNNs powered the modern computer-vision revolution. They remain central in vision pipelines even as Transformers gain ground.

explainer.lead: A convolutional neural network learns small pattern detectors that it reuses across an image or another grid. This makes it especially good at turning raw pixels into increasingly useful visual features, from simple edges to whole objects.

tiers.eli5: It's like scanning a picture with a small magnifying glass that moves across it, learning to spot simple edges first and then whole objects.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use CNNs in vision pipelines, relying on shared weights to cut parameters and build features layer by layer. A pitfall is assuming Transformers have displaced them; CNNs remain central in vision pipelines.
tiers.paperLevel: A neural network whose learned filters slide over the input, sharing weights across spatial locations and building hierarchical features; LeNet demonstrated the approach on handwritten digits. Known limits are tied to grid-structured input assumptions.

components.name: Input grid
components.detail: The image or other spatially arranged data entering the network.

components.name: Learned filters
components.detail: Small sets of weights that detect local patterns wherever they occur.

components.name: Feature maps
components.detail: The responses produced as filters slide across their inputs.

components.name: Layer hierarchy
components.detail: Successive layers combine early edge-like features into higher-level object features.

flow: An image or other grid enters the network.
Each learned filter slides across the grid, reusing the same weights at every location.
The filter responses form feature maps for the next layer.
Later layers combine earlier features into increasingly high-level representations.

explainer.whyItMatters: Weight sharing lets a CNN learn local patterns once and recognize them across an entire input. Its hierarchical features made neural networks especially effective for vision.

diagram.caption: Shared filters turn grid inputs into feature maps, which deeper layers combine into a visual hierarchy.

explainer.example: A CNN detects edges in early layers and whole objects in later layers when classifying images, with LeNet as the classic handwritten-digit demonstration.
